headline: Over 5 lakh fail as HSC pass rate hits 22-year low
summary: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate exams dropped to 51.62%, marking the lowest result in over two decades.
details: The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with more than five lakh students failing under the nine general education boards.
The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, down from 57.12 percent last year, according to results published on Saturday.

An analysis of historical data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS) shows that the last time the pass rate was lower than this year was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.
This year, 5,07,281 of the 10,48,530 examinees under the nine general education boards failed, compared with 4,49,076 last year.
Across all 11 education boards, including the Madrasa and Technical education boards, 5,94,113 students failed, and the combined pass rate stood at 52.12 percent.
The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also fell to an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government would take steps to address learning gaps.

headline_marked: 30+ factories shut as [[RMG workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage]]
headline: 30+ factories shut as RMG workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage
summary: Protests in Ashulia and Mirpur led to road blockades and clashes with police, with workers demanding a minimum monthly wage and an end to blacklisting.
details: At least 30 garment factories in the Kathgara area of Ashulia have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The unrest began in the morning, leading to road blockades in Ashulia and Dhaka's Mirpur area. Protesters allegedly threw bricks and stones at factories, resulting in chases and counter-chases between workers and police.

A police officer was hospitalized after being struck on the head by bricks. Additionally, industrial police recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area.

Workers are also demanding an end to blacklisting and a halt to arbitrary dismissals. The Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre stated that anger grew after the government failed to form a wage board by October as previously announced.
The Ministry of Labour announced that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, but workers continue to protest as the message has not been properly conveyed to them.
caption:
30+ garment factories shut down as workers take to the streets demanding a Tk 30,000 minimum wage.

At least 30 garment factories in the Kathgara area of Ashulia have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The unrest began in the morning, leading to road blockades in Ashulia and Dhaka's Mirpur area. Protesters allegedly threw bricks and stones at factories, resulting in chases and counter-chases between workers and police.

A police officer was hospitalized after being struck on the head by bricks. Additionally, industrial police recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area.

Workers are also demanding an end to blacklisting and a halt to arbitrary dismissals. The Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre stated that anger grew after the government failed to form a wage board by October as previously announced.

The Ministry of Labour announced that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, but workers continue to protest as the message has not been properly conveyed to them.
